claims.claim: The physical and spiritual equations share the same functional form.
claims.plain_english: The math that describes the physical world and the math that describes spiritual truths are actually the same equation.
claims.evidence_given: The document asserts a 'visual proof' placing the equations side by side, but provides no actual equations or derivations in this interlude.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the two equations have different mathematical structures when written out in full, the claim would be false.

claims.claim: The same slot changes every time, and the free-will term is the tell.
claims.plain_english: There is a variable in the equation that always changes, and that variable represents free will.
claims.evidence_given: Repeated as a pull quote and verdict, but no derivation or example is given in this interlude.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the changing slot can be explained by deterministic factors rather than free will, or if no such slot exists in the actual equations.

claims.claim: The repeated structure between physical and spiritual equations is unavoidable once placed side by side.
claims.plain_english: If you look at both equations together, you can't miss that they are built the same way.
claims.evidence_given: The document states this as a premise but does not show the equations or the side-by-side comparison in this interlude.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the equations, when written out, do not share a repeated structure, or if the similarity is coincidental and not meaningful.

claims.claim: The equations do not merely rhyme; they share the same functional form.
claims.plain_english: It's not just that the equations look similar—they are mathematically identical in structure.
claims.evidence_given: The document poses this as the central question but does not provide the mathematical proof in this interlude.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the equations are only analogous (rhyme) rather than isomorphic (same form), the claim would be false.

claims.claim: The visual proof is sufficient to make the repeated structure unavoidable.
claims.plain_english: Just by looking at the equations side by side, you will be forced to see they are the same.
claims.evidence_given: The document claims this but does not present the visual proof in this interlude.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a reader can view both equations and reasonably conclude they are not the same structure.

claims.claim: The free-will term is the key difference between the physical and spiritual equations.
claims.plain_english: The only thing that changes between the two equations is a term that represents free will.
claims.evidence_given: Stated as a pull quote and verdict, but no explanation of what the free-will term is or how it functions is given.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the difference between the equations can be explained without invoking free will, or if free will is not a meaningful variable in the equations.

claims.claim: The interlude sends the reader to the canonical page instead of replacing it.
claims.plain_english: This page is just a summary; the full proof is on another page.
claims.evidence_given: The document explicitly states this multiple times and provides links to the canonical page.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the canonical page does not exist or does not contain the promised proof.
